Malogoszcz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Małogoszcz, Poland

Not demolished. Małogoszcz's Jews were barred from settling there between 1775 and 1862, living instead mainly in surrounding villages; once restrictions lifted, the community grew rapidly, reaching 1,050 people by 1938. A ghetto established in 1941 saw about 830 people deported to Treblinka upon its August 1942 liquidation, with about 300 more sent to the Jędrzejów Ghetto and a labor camp before also reaching Auschwitz. This cemetery, established in 1882 and enlarged in 1925, was enclosed with a stone wall between 1929 and 1932; about 70 surviving matzevot, made of Chęciny marble, limestone, conglomerate, and sandstone, remain largely in their original burial positions, preserving the cemetery's traditional division between male and female sections.
